tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the expected future tax consequences attributable to differences between financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax bases and operating loss and other loss carryforwards. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. The Company records a valuation allowance that primarily represents non-U.S. operating and other loss carryforwards for which realization is uncertain. Management judgment is required in determining the Company’s provision for income taxes, deferred tax assets and liabilities, and the valuation allowance recorded against the Company’s net deferred tax assets.

The Company reviews the realizability of its deferred tax assets and related valuation allowances on a quarterly basis, or whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that a review is required. In determining the requirement for a valuation allowance, the historical and projected financial results of the legal entity or consolidated group recording the net deferred tax asset are considered, along with any other positive or negative evidence.

da.text: The Company performs impairment reviews for its reporting units, which have been determined to be one level below the Company's operating segments, using a qualitative assessment or a quantitative test. A qualitative assessment is performed when prior quantitative assessments have resulted in significant excess of fair value over the carrying value of a reporting unit, and consideration of qualitative factors allow the Company to conclude it is more likely than not that the fair value of the reporting unit remains greater than its carrying value. When performing a quantitative goodwill impairment test, the fair value of a reporting unit refers to the price that would be received to sell the unit as a whole in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. To estimate the fair value, the Company uses a discounted cash flow model, the guideline company method under the market approach, or estimated sales price for reporting units held for sale. The assumptions included in the impairment tests require judgment, and changes to these inputs could impact the results of the calculations. The key assumptions used in the impairment tests were management's projections of future cash flows, earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (“EBITDA”), weighted-average cost of capital, EBITDA multiples, and long-term growth rates.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Income taxes payable, non-current
lines.why: Taxes on operating income due after a year (often uncertain tax positions): operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: In fiscal 2026, products and systems accounted for approximately 69% of sales from continuing operations and services accounted for 31% of sales from continuing operations.
In fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024, no customer exceeded 10% of consolidated net sales.

The Company could experience further disruptions, shortages, tariffs and price inflation in the future, the effect of which will depend on the Company’s ability to successfully mitigate and offset the impact of these events.

An increasing portion of the demand growth for our commercial HVAC products is driven by data center customers whose investment decisions depend on the pace of artificial intelligence adoption and the capital expenditure plans of a limited number of hyperscale technology companies.
Our results of operations and continued growth rely on delivering differentiated solutions in key growth verticals, particularly through our direct channel sales.
The direct channel provides for the installation of fire and security solutions, and HVAC equipment manufactured by us.

Further, our ability to grow and maintain our service business depends on our ability to provide differentiated products and services through our technology and expertise to achieve desired customer outcomes in our key growth verticals.
The implementation of our operating model also depends on our ability to quickly respond to market and innovation driven changes and redeploy our resources as needed within our organization.

system depends on our ability to train our employees on the business system and processes, hire and retain key personnel involved in the implementation, and manage organizational change across a large, geographically dispersed workforce.

Because not all of our business arrangements provide for guaranteed supply and some key parts require long qualification periods or may be available only from a single supplier or a limited group of suppliers, we are subject to supply and pricing risk.
We could experience the recurrence of similar or new disruptions in the future, the effect of which will depend on our ability to successfully mitigate the impact of these disruptions.
Our business success depends on attracting and retaining qualified personnel.
We rely on the capacity, reliability and security of our IT and data security infrastructure, and on our ability to expand and update it as our business changes.

Certain of our AI capabilities may depend on third-party models, platforms and service providers whose performance, availability, security, policies or regulatory compliance may adversely affect our business, operations or results.
We rely on a combination of trademarks, trade secrets, patents, copyrights, know-how, confidentiality provisions and licensing arrangements to protect our proprietary rights.
For those products in our portfolio that rely on patent protection, once a patent has expired, the product is generally open to competition.
The net effect of these actions will depend on our ability to successfully mitigate and offset their impact, which may not be effective.

The timing, declaration and payment of future dividends to holders of the Company’s ordinary shares will depend upon many factors, including the Company’s financial condition and results of operations, the capital requirements of its businesses, industry practice and any other relevant factors.
The continued net effect of these events will depend on the Company’s ability to successfully mitigate and offset their impacts.

The extent to which the Company’s results of operations and financial condition are impacted by these and other factors in the future will depend on developments that are highly uncertain and cannot be predicted.

The Company believes the percentage of net debt to net capitalization is useful to understanding the Company’s financial condition as it provides a view of the extent to which the Company relies on external debt financing for its funding and is a measure of risk to its shareholders.

The timing, declaration and payment of future dividends to holders of the Company's ordinary shares is determined by the Company's Board of Directors and depends upon many factors, including the Company's financial condition and results of operations, the capital requirements of the Company's businesses, industry practice and any other relevant factors.
Purchases or retirement of debt, if any, will depend on prevailing market conditions, liquidity requirements, contractual restrictions and other factors.
